cohort: 1274 primigravidae women under the age of 40 years who underwent induced labor at term
finding: Increasing BMI was independently associated with increased odds of cesarean section and lower Apgar scores in women with induced labor.
mod_finding: Women who were overweight and obese had a 1.58 and 2.75 times greater likelihood of having a cesarean section, respectively, compared to women with normal BMI.
